objects.docstring:
poetry-motion: opt-in animated effects. The server renders each
effect's finished state; the vendored animation engine
(`@poetry/motion/engine`) is pinned without preload and fetched by a
dynamic import the first time an element asks for it, so a page with no
motion element loads none of it. One policy module
(`@poetry/motion/policy`) owns reduced motion, the motion tokens, the
Turbo cache flush and the one view-transition slot.

objects.docstring:
A list whose Turbo Stream changes animate: appended items fade in,
removed items fade out, and the rest slide to their new places. The
server renders the list as it is, and a stream's own render does
the change; the effect only animates it, as a layout transition.

examples.text:
<%= poetry_animated_list(id: "comments") do %>
  <%= render @comments %>
<% end %>
<%# a turbo_stream.append "comments" from the server now animates %>

bursts nothing.

Content you can pick up and move - a sticker, a playful card. It
follows the drag, within its parent's box when bounded:, and springs
home on release unless snap_back: false leaves it where it was

motion; only the spring home is skipped. Where it lands is not
saved: the server renders it in place.

A row (or column) of items that scrolls in a loop, logos or
testimonials. The loop is CSS, so no engine loads. The server
renders the items once for readers and `repeat:` copies for the
loop, aria-hidden and inert. Hover and focus inside pause it, and a
pause control holds it still (WCAG 2.2.2). Under reduced motion it
stands still and only the readable copy shows.

examples.text:
<%= poetry_marquee(label: "Our customers") do %>
  <% customers.each do |customer| %><%= image_tag customer.logo, alt: customer.name %><% end %>
<% end %>

The motion options an effect declares, each validated against the
motion tokens: an effect calls `motion_options` with the options it
takes and their defaults, and every effect also gets `animate:` to
turn its motion off.

The values reach the effect's controller as Stimulus values, and the
motion policy reads the tokens they name.

One element on two pages: give it the same name on both, and a Turbo
visit between them morphs it from one place to the other (a card
into its detail page, a thumbnail into the hero). It is a

view-transition meta tag in your layout. Reduced motion swaps the
pages without the morph. No script.

A stack of cards to swipe through, one decision each: drag the top
card left or right past the threshold, press the arrow keys on the
focused stack, or wire your own buttons to swipeLeft and swipeRight.
with_actions renders inside the stack, so its buttons reach the
controller. Each swipe dispatches poetry--motion--swipe-cards:swipe with
{ direction, card, index }; record it there (a form post, a Turbo
Stream). When the last card goes, the with_empty content shows.

examples.text:
<%= poetry_swipe_cards(label: "Candidates") do |stack| %>
  <% candidates.each do |candidate| %>
    <% stack.with_card(data: { id: candidate.id }) { render candidate } %>
  <% end %>
  <% stack.with_empty { "That's everyone." } %>
  <% stack.with_actions do %>
    <%= poetry_button(variant: :outline,
                      data: { action: "poetry--motion--swipe-cards#swipeLeft" }) { "Skip" } %>
    <%= poetry_button(data: { action: "poetry--motion--swipe-cards#swipeRight" }) { "Keep" } %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>

custom property; under reduced motion the text is simply there.

A surface that leans toward a fine pointer and springs back flat
when it leaves. It wraps whatever it is given, a poetry Card most
often. The lean rotates an inner layer, never the outer element,
and the server renders the card flat; touch, coarse pointers and
reduced motion leave it that way.

A word that turns over into the next, in place: "Build faster",
"Build safer". The words are server-rendered and stacked in one cell
sized to the longest, so the line never reflows; the first shows,
and a screen reader hears only it. Hover and focus pause it, and it
stops after its rounds, back on the first word.
